releases.title: Visible AI work, explainable numbers and a clearer Case Manager
releases.summary: Everything since 0.1.1 in one release, under a new repository identity and the Apache-2.0 license.

updates.title: Visible AI work, explainable numbers and a clearer Case Manager

highlights.title: See when the AI is working on a case
highlights.summary: The queue, the case header, the navigation and the close dialogs show when an AI investigation is running or waiting.
details: The case header shows **AI working** with the time so far, or **AI queued**. Its popover says who started the run.
The Case Manager item in the navigation counts the cases the AI is working on.
The run's result stays authoritative. A close made while it runs is replaced by its result, and the close dialogs say so before you act.
When a run you started finishes, or a run replaces your close, your Inbox tells you.

screenshot.alt: Case header with the AI working chip and its popover open, titled AI investigation running, saying You started it, with the time the run has taken so far.
screenshot.caption: The AI working chip and its popover.

highlights.title: A clearer Case Manager
highlights.summary: Each part of a case has one place. The header takes two lines, the case facts sit in their own column, and the queue folds away when you need the width.
details: The header's second line keeps the case number, severity, status, risk, AI verdict, owner and SLA on one line.
Press **]** to show or hide the case facts. In a narrow pane they open in a side sheet.
Press **[** to fold the queue into a narrow strip. J and K still move through the cases.
The Brief opens with the case's next step and four lanes: Evidence, AI, Decision and People.

screenshot.alt: Case Manager with the queue on the left, one row marked AI working, and an open case with its two-line header, the six tabs and the case facts column on the right.
screenshot.caption: The Case Manager in this update.

highlights.title: A new repository identity for updates
highlights.summary: Signed updates now come from ARYDESTROYER/Kavach-AgenticSOC. Set it in .env before you bootstrap the updater.
details: Add `AGENTIC_SOC_UPDATE_REPOSITORY=ARYDESTROYER/Kavach-AgenticSOC` to .env, with that exact letter case.
The bootstrap refuses a missing line or the former name, prints the line to add, and never edits .env.
Releases 0.1.12 and earlier stay valid under the former name. The public Help Center moved to the new Pages address.

screenshot.alt: Updates and releases settings with the Public repository field set to the ARYDESTROYER/Kavach-AgenticSOC GitHub address and the Stable and Testing branch fields below it.
screenshot.caption: The new repository identity in Settings.

highlights.title: Case tabs in a new order
highlights.summary: Six tabs: Brief, Evidence, AI investigation, Response, Activity and Chat. Alt+2, Alt+4 and Alt+5 now open Evidence, Response and Activity, and Chat moves to Alt+6.
details: Alt+1 to Alt+6 open the tabs in that order.
Before, Alt+2 opened Runbook, Alt+4 opened Collaboration and Alt+5 opened Chat.
A link to the retired Timeline or Threat context tab opens Evidence at the matching section.

screenshot.alt: Brief tab of a case under the six tabs Brief, Evidence, AI investigation, Response, Activity and Chat, with the Next step row above the Evidence, AI, Decision and People lanes.
screenshot.caption: The six case tabs, with the Brief open.

highlights.title: Every number shows its math
highlights.summary: Hover a risk score, a decision or a dashboard figure for its formula with the real numbers. Press it for the inputs, the steps and the rounding.
details: On a case: the risk score, the close or escalate decision, the priority, the SLA and the AI cost.
On dashboards and Metrics: the KPI figures, with the cases behind them.
**Copy calculation** copies the whole arithmetic.
A case scored before this version keeps its stored factors. Where its inputs were not kept, the panel says they were not recorded.

screenshot.alt: Risk score panel for one case listing each factor, its weight and its value, the weighted sum, the rounding and the total, with a Copy calculation button.
screenshot.caption: The risk score with its math.

highlights.title: What's new and Communication
highlights.summary: This welcome appears once after each update. The Communication group holds Inbox and What's new, the release tracker.
details: Open **Communication**, then **What's new**, to read every release with its highlights and screenshots.
Turn the welcome off with **Show What's new after updates** in Settings, Account, Appearance.

screenshot.alt: Communication, What's new page with the version rail listing 0.2.0 and 0.1.1, the 0.2.0 release summary, area filters and the newest update's highlights.
screenshot.caption: The release tracker in Communication.

highlights.title: A quieter sign-in page
highlights.summary: The sign-in page uses the Console's own colours and moves once as it opens. The Remember me row shows only its name.
details: Checking **Remember me** opens a warning first. It says how long this device stays signed in.
When an administrator turned Remember me off, or the connection is not secure, the row stays visible and disabled, with the reason.
A single sign-on error shows a fixed sentence, never text from the address bar.

screenshot.alt: Sign-in page at the password step with the masked password field, a Remember me checkbox with no duration, and the Sign in button.
screenshot.caption: The sign-in page.

highlights.title: Every case record within reach
highlights.summary: The Evidence tab lists the raw events behind a case. The case facts open every stored field and each AI call with its cost.
details: Open an event for every field as a table or as JSON, then copy or download it.
**View all fields** in the case facts shows every stored field of the case.
The cost in the case facts lists each AI call with its tokens and its cost formula.
Raw events need the `sources:read` permission. AI costs need `cost:view`.

screenshot.alt: Case facts with the View all fields sheet open, showing every stored field of the case as a searchable tree with Copy JSON and Download buttons.

highlights.title: Access and account security fixes
highlights.summary: Case reads, the settings read and Standup now check permissions, and account security is stricter.
details: A role without the permission now gets an Access denied answer from these reads.
An account an administrator creates or resets must change its temporary password before anything else.
Ten wrong second-factor codes in a row pause second-factor checks for 5 minutes, doubling up to an hour.
Changing your own password signs out your other sessions. An administrator's reset signs the account out everywhere.
Only a Super admin with a fresh sign-in can change single sign-on settings.
Single sign-on no longer links an account created through another provider because the email matches.

highlights.title: Fixes across the application
highlights.summary: Fixes from a full review of the application, in the AI pipeline, SLA timers, metrics, settings, Demo Mode and accessibility.
details: A case a person closed before an automatic AI run started stays closed.
The SLA response clock stops for a case the AI agent closed.
Settings refuses values that cannot work together, such as a response target longer than the resolution target.
In Demo Mode, a seeded case's cost has usage rows behind it, and its risk score matches its factors.
Focus, names and reflow work better with a keyboard, a screen reader and a phone.

highlights.title: Apache-2.0 license
highlights.summary: Agentic SOC is free software under the Apache License 2.0.
details: The license text is in the repository and in each image.

updates.title: Team activity, case screenshots and a calmer Case Manager

highlights.title: Team activity
highlights.summary: Per-person, per-day work counts from the audit log, for SOC managers and auditors.
details: Counts come with their context. The page never ranks people or gives them a score.
A chart per day, a sheet for each person with their events, and a CSV download.

highlights.title: Screenshots on cases
highlights.summary: Add PNG, JPEG or WebP screenshots to a case. Their metadata is removed and they are never sent to a model.
details: Paste, drag and drop or pick a file, with an optional caption.
Up to 20 images per case, 2 MiB each and 20 MiB per case.

highlights.title: A review of automatic closes
highlights.summary: About 5% of automatic closes are picked for a person to review, at most 10 a day and 3 per rule.
details: You classify the case before you see what the AI decided.
A review never changes the case unless you reopen it.
Reviews stay out of agent statistics. Agent effectiveness shows the agreement once 30 reviews exist.

highlights.title: A calmer Case Manager
highlights.summary: One control band above the queue, two-line queue rows, and one primary action for the case's state beside Take action.
details: The queue gains a Review scope with the number of reviews waiting.

screenshot.alt: Case Manager in Demo Mode with the Active, Mine, Review and All scopes above two-line queue rows, and an escalated case open with Mark resolved, Take action and five tabs, Investigation selected.
screenshot.caption: The Case Manager in this update.

highlights.title: A clearer close
highlights.summary: Closing a case asks for the disposition once and can record the actions taken. Rate the AI starts collapsed.
details: A note is asked for only when your classification overrides the AI.

highlights.title: A switch for role-based access
highlights.summary: A Super admin turns role-based access on or off on Roles and permissions, after a fresh sign-in.

screenshot.alt: Roles and permissions section of Settings with the Role-based access group at the top: its Enforcement row reads Off, every signed-in account is treated as Super admin, and the Turn on role-based access button is outlined, above the table of six built-in roles.
screenshot.caption: The Role-based access group in this update.

highlights.title: Truthful setup wording
highlights.summary: The setup wizard says Ready for live triage only when a source is connected and the investigation models can be called.
details: Without a usable key it says so, and that new cases wait for a person.

screenshot.alt: Setup wizard AI runtime stage with the amber notice No usable AI provider yet, which says you can continue without a key but new cases wait for a person as Needs human review, above empty OpenAI, Anthropic and Embedding API key fields marked not set, and a Skip for now button.
screenshot.caption: The setup wizard's AI runtime stage in this update.

highlights.title: Only a Super admin manages Super admin accounts
highlights.summary: Giving an account the Super admin role, or changing one that has it, needs a Super admin with a recent sign-in.

highlights.title: Reinvestigation keeps people's work
highlights.summary: Rebuilding a case keeps its owner, comments, grades, history and a disposition an analyst set.

updates.title: A step-by-step install guide with real screenshots

highlights.title: A step-by-step install guide
highlights.summary: The Install and First-run setup pages walk through every step with real screenshots of each first-run screen.
details: The repository's install guide covers five paths: a workstation demo, the Compose stack, production hardening, an existing Elastic stack and running from source.

screenshot.alt: First-run screen titled Create your admin account, with the admin username, display name, password and confirm password fields filled and the Create admin and sign in button below.
screenshot.caption: One of the first-run screens the guide shows.

highlights.title: Architecture diagrams
highlights.summary: Light and dark diagrams show the system data flow and the Compose deployment.

updates.title: Steadier runbook guidance and audit log fixes

highlights.title: The fallback runbook no longer guides the AI
highlights.summary: The Generic incident fallback runbook is still attached for people, but it no longer guides the investigator. A specific runbook still does.
details: Guidance can change the verdict the AI returns, never the close decision.

highlights.title: The audit log reads every row on PostgreSQL
highlights.summary: A stray control character in an audit row no longer breaks the Audit log, its count, its exports or chat's audit search.

highlights.title: Your account activity is back
highlights.summary: Settings, Account, Sessions and activity shows your own events again.

highlights.title: Safer rollbacks
highlights.summary: This build keeps what a newer build writes, so a later release can roll back to it cleanly.

updates.title: A Dashboards library, a usable audit log, rule sheets and Runbooks

highlights.title: Dashboards library
highlights.summary: The Overview row opens a library of four built-in dashboards and your own. The Cyber Defence Center stays the landing page.
details: Built-in dashboards are read only. Duplicate one to change it.

screenshot.alt: Dashboards library with four built-in dashboards, the Cyber Defence Center marked Default, and the user's own dashboards below.
screenshot.caption: The Dashboards library in this update.

highlights.title: An audit log you can use
highlights.summary: Search the audit log, choose a scope, open any record in a side sheet, and export CSV or JSON Lines.
details: Export needs the `audit:export` permission and a fresh sign-in.

screenshot.alt: Audit log page with time range, scope tabs, search and filters above a table of audited events with time, outcome, event, actor, target and summary.
screenshot.caption: The Audit log in this update.

highlights.title: A sheet for every rule
highlights.summary: Press any rule name to see its alerts over time, its top sources and targets, and its latest alerts and cases, with Open all in Logs.

highlights.title: One Runbooks feature
highlights.summary: Phased procedures with matching that gives its reason, a run on each case with a Next step card, and reviewed versions.
details: A library of 12 built-in runbooks.
The investigator reads only Published runbook text.

screenshot.alt: Runbooks library with run statistics and a table of twelve published built-in runbooks such as Brute force and password spray.
screenshot.caption: The Runbooks library in this update.

highlights.title: The Console offers only what your roles allow
highlights.summary: Pages, panels and actions your roles cannot use are not offered, because the Console reads the server's own access check.

highlights.title: Named severity levels
highlights.summary: Severity breakdowns use named levels, with the top rules and Split by.

highlights.title: Docked navigation and grouped Settings
highlights.summary: The navigation rail docks beside every page, and Settings is grouped.

highlights.title: More room for chat
highlights.summary: The default chat timeouts and capacity are three times larger.

updates.title: Suggested questions and a neater chat

highlights.title: Suggested questions from your data
highlights.summary: A new chat offers 3 or 4 questions built from your own cases and sources, with no model call.
details: Each suggestion has a one-line reason, and a line says what changed since your last visit.
Hide a suggestion for a day, or turn suggestions off in the composer options.

highlights.title: Follow-up questions
highlights.summary: After an answer, up to three follow-up questions appear, each naming something the answer shows.

screenshot.alt: Workspace Chat at the end of an answer about new cases, showing a new-cases-by-severity table with top rules, the answer's lookups, time and simulated cost, and three suggested follow-up questions.
screenshot.caption: An answer with follow-up questions in this update.

highlights.title: Conversation titles
highlights.summary: A conversation takes its title from the first answer.

highlights.title: A neater reading column
highlights.summary: Answers sit in a narrower reading column, with quieter block headers and the cost on the meta row.

updates.title: Chat without limits, Remember me and report downloads

highlights.title: Chat without per-question caps
highlights.summary: A question runs until it is answered, with loop guards instead of caps. Chat sits outside the daily and monthly AI budget.
details: An optional chat-only daily cap is off by default.
Every chat call is still recorded in the cost ledger.

highlights.title: A working indicator you can come back to
highlights.summary: The navigation shows when chat is working. Leave the page and come back to the live answer.

highlights.title: Remember me
highlights.summary: Stay signed in on this device for a time your administrator bounds.

highlights.title: Report downloads
highlights.summary: Reports download reliably, now also as Word and Excel files.

highlights.title: Exact counts in chat and dashboards
highlights.summary: Chat counts cases exactly over any window, all time and calendar periods included. Dashboards read exact totals.

highlights.title: Overview and Case Manager redesigns
highlights.summary: The Overview and the Case Manager were redesigned, and a closed case shows the analyst's classification first.

screenshot.alt: Cyber Defence Center dashboard with case KPIs, a noise reduction flow from alerts to cases, and a human versus AI chart.
screenshot.caption: The Cyber Defence Center after the redesign.

highlights.title: Workspace chat
highlights.summary: A read-only assistant that looks things up for you and answers with blocks, citations and reports.
details: One question can run several read-only lookups, and the page shows each one as it runs.
A live token meter shows what each answer costs.

highlights.title: Reports
highlights.summary: Collect answers into a report with your notes and an optional AI summary. The Reports library lists them.

updates.title: KPI drill-downs, Agent health in the bell and a navy dark mode

highlights.title: A drill-down behind every KPI
highlights.summary: Press a KPI tile to see the cases behind the number. Switch metrics in place and download the rows as CSV.

highlights.title: An Auto-closed tile
highlights.summary: A sixth KPI tile shows the cases the AI agent closed automatically, a part of Resolved or closed.

highlights.title: Agent health in the notification bell
highlights.summary: Agent health sits at the top of the notification bell, so a problem shows on every page.

highlights.title: A deep navy dark mode
highlights.summary: Dark mode moved to a deep navy palette, with every contrast pair measured again.

highlights.title: A close records your classification
highlights.summary: When you choose a disposition as you close a case, it counts as your classification. The AI's own label never counts as yours.

highlights.title: The investigator sees the fields that matter
highlights.summary: The investigator now reads alert fields such as the URL path, the HTTP method and the user agent.

updates.title: Cyber Defence Center and required MFA

highlights.title: Cyber Defence Center
highlights.summary: The landing dashboard has a new name, and every metric shows a trendline on hover or focus.

highlights.title: Human vs AI
highlights.summary: A Human vs AI card shows how many cases people and the AI agent closed over time.

highlights.title: Multi-factor sign-in an administrator can require
highlights.summary: An administrator can require multi-factor sign-in for an account. The person enrols while signing in.

highlights.title: Richer account creation
highlights.summary: Set a display name, email, phone and custom roles when you create an account, with a live summary of the role.

screenshot.alt: Add user dialog with a username, full name, masked temporary password and the Analyst Tier 1 role with its permission summary.
screenshot.caption: The Add user dialog.

highlights.title: 38 enrichment providers
highlights.summary: 19 new enrichment providers, each with setup steps and an example on its card.

highlights.title: Authenticator QR codes that scan
highlights.summary: The QR code for authenticator setup now follows the standard, so every scanner reads it.

updates.title: Background jobs, a full data export and declared-benign rules

highlights.title: Background jobs
highlights.summary: Long work runs as a background job that keeps going when you leave the page. Analytics, Jobs shows its progress and lets you cancel it.
details: A job's file downloads only after the server has verified it.
Inbox tells you when a job finishes.

highlights.title: A full data export
highlights.summary: Settings, Organization, Data export builds one verified ZIP of the scopes you choose, on the server.

highlights.title: Declare a rule benign
highlights.summary: Declare a detection rule benign in your environment. Its alerts then close with no model call, within a risk ceiling, a scope and an expiry you set.
details: Reinvestigating a case always overrides the declaration for that case, and a person's work is never closed over.

highlights.title: Analyst-confirmed precedent
highlights.summary: When you turn it on, the investigator is told how many cases of the same rule analysts confirmed. The verdict stays the model's.

highlights.title: Simple and Detailed noise reduction views
highlights.summary: The noise reduction flow has a Simple view of the whole alert-to-case flow and a Detailed view.

highlights.title: A provider outage cannot empty the knowledge corpus
highlights.summary: A rebuild that would empty the knowledge corpus is refused, and health reads Degraded while the corpus is empty.

highlights.title: Signed, supervised updates
highlights.summary: On the PostgreSQL Compose deployment, a Super admin installs a newer Stable release after a signed preflight that can roll back.

highlights.title: Bootstrap from 0.1.1
highlights.summary: Bootstrapping the updater from 0.1.1 no longer stops on application images that carry no state-schema label.

releases.title: The first Stable release of the 0.1 line
releases.summary: Vendor-neutral ingestion, a tiered AI investigation, decisions made by code, an audit trail and a cost ledger.

highlights.title: Pull and push sources, normalised to OCSF
highlights.summary: Elasticsearch, OpenSearch and Wazuh pull connectors, plus a broad catalog of push, queue and object store receivers. Every record is normalised to OCSF.
details: Durable cursors, so no event is skipped or read twice.
Correlation and risk scoring by code, and one case per cluster signature.

highlights.title: A tiered AI investigation
highlights.summary: A router model and an investigator model look into each case. Every model call goes through one gateway into the cost ledger.

highlights.title: Decisions made by code
highlights.summary: Code closes or escalates a case against the policy you set. Neither the model nor procedure text can override it.
details: A case that needs a human never closes automatically, and closing a true positive automatically is off by default.
A daily AI budget of 10 US dollars blocks further calls by default. A blocked call sends the case to a person.

highlights.title: Case Manager
highlights.summary: A split-pane queue beside the case workspace, with traces, rationale, collaboration and feedback.
details: Bulk work is checked against each person's permissions.
The 0.1 line also brought campaigns, entity baselines, threshold tuning, detection rules and custom dashboards.

highlights.title: Security Command Center
highlights.summary: The landing dashboard showed case KPIs, active risk, noise reduction and response timing, with a live refresh.

highlights.title: Workspace Chat
highlights.summary: A personal chat with saved, searchable conversations. Case Manager chat uses the same read-only engine for one case.

highlights.title: Sign-in, roles and single sign-on
highlights.summary: Local sign-in, sessions, role-based access with custom roles, authenticator codes and single sign-on with OpenID Connect.

highlights.title: Your choice of state store
highlights.summary: PostgreSQL with pgvector, Elasticsearch or SQLite holds the application's own state.

highlights.title: Demo Mode and the Help Center
highlights.summary: An isolated Demo Mode with five synthetic sources, and a Help Center that matches the installed version.
